traceability.evidence:
Story file: - docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md exists and is referenced throughout implementation and tests via @story annotations.
Core rules: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts implements the ESLint rule `require-story-annotation`. - Uses shared helpers from src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers and src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors. - meta.schema defines options: `scope` (array of DEFAULT_SCOPE node types) and `exportPriority` (enum of EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES). - create(context) reads options, defaults `scope` and `exportPriority`, and delegates to buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode, scope, exportPriority }). - Error message `missingStory` explicitly names the function and describes how to add an @story annotation, including an example story path. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts implements the ESLint rule `require-req-annotation`. - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, and shouldProcessNode from ./helpers/require-story-helpers and checkReqAnnotation from ../utils/annotation-checker. - meta.schema mirrors require-story-annotation: same `scope` and `exportPriority` semantics and defaults. - create(context) normalizes options (scope falls back to DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority to "all"), defines shouldCheck(node) with shouldProcessNode, and for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature, calls checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) when in scope.
Shared detection, scope, and export semantics: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - export const DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]. - export const EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - Re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - isExportedNode(node): walks parent chain to detect ExportNamedDeclaration / ExportDefaultDeclaration. - shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority = "all"): requires node.type in scope, then applies exportPriority semantics (all/exported/non-exported). - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts: - Provides visitors for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature, and ArrowFunctionExpression, each calling options.shouldProcessNode(node) before reporting. - Because DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include "ArrowFunctionExpression" and the rule options schema restricts scope values to DEFAULT_SCOPE, arrow functions are excluded from enforcement by default, matching the story requirement. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts visitors cover the same function-like node kinds (excluding ArrowFunctionExpression), gated by the same shouldProcessNode logic via DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority. → Together this satisfies REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, and REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY consistently across both rules.
JSDoc/comment parsing and error handling (@story): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node), commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node), and leadingCommentsHasStory(node) inspect JSDoc, getCommentsBefore, and leadingComments for "@story". - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) composes these with: - linesBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node, LOOKBACK_LINES), - parentChainHasStory(sourceCode, node), - fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node), all imported from src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts, and wrapped in try/catch to fail gracefully on malformed input. - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?) and reportMethod(...) compute function/method names, skip when hasStoryAnnotation is true, and report with messageId "missingStory" anchored on the identifier/key node, including data { name, functionName } and auto-fix suggestions using createAddStoryFix/createMethodFix. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts safely implements linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, and fallbackTextBeforeHasStory with guards on sourceCode, loc, and range plus try/catch, satisfying the error-handling criterion for malformed comments and edge cases.
JSDoc/comment parsing and error handling (@req): - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts: - getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, and combineComments encapsulate retrieval of JSDoc and surrounding comments. - getFixTargetNode and createMissingReqFix implement autofix insertion points for @req; require-req-annotation disables autofix via enableFix: false. - reportMissing(context, node, enableFix) uses getNodeName to derive a readable function name, anchors errors on the function id/key, and reports messageId "missingReq" with data { name, functionName }, optionally attaching an autofix. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix }) acquires sourceCode from context, computes jsdoc and comments arrays, calls hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node), and reports only when no @req is found. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts (hasReqAnnotation and helpers): - Reuses LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW from src/rules/helpers/require-story-io. - linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq each guard against malformed data and are wrapped in try/catch; fallback detection scans a bounded text window before the node for "@req". - hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node) combines these heuristics and finally falls back to simple jsdoc.value.includes("@req") or comments.some(commentContainsReq), satisfying REQ-JSDOC-PARSING and error-handling requirements for @req.
TypeScript support: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts includes TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature visitors for require-story-annotation. - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts includes TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature handlers that delegate to checkReqAnnotation. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts are designed to work with TypeScript nodes via context.getSourceCode, loc, range, comments, and dedicated TS tests. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts defines a RuleTester-based pseudo-rule that calls checkReqAnnotation on TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature, and verifies both detection and autofix behavior for missing @req, demonstrating TS support in isolation.
User-facing documentation: - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md: - Describes rule behavior and explicitly lists supported node types (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) and notes that arrow functions are not in scope via options. - Documents options `scope` and `exportPriority` in prose and JSON schema, including defaults. - Provides correct and incorrect examples for JavaScript and TypeScript declarations and method signatures. - docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md: - States that it enforces `@req` on the same kinds of nodes as require-story-annotation and explicitly documents the shared semantics for `scope` and `exportPriority`. - Lists supported node types including TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature and explicitly notes that arrow functions are not checked. - Includes detailed correct/incorrect examples for JS and TS.
Tests (RuleTester coverage with story traceability): - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts: - JSDoc header: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`. - Uses RuleTester plus withTsLanguageOptions for TS cases. - valid tests include: - FunctionDeclaration and FunctionExpression with @story in JSDoc or line comments. - Class method, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature with @story. - Arrow function with @story. - Unannotated arrow function allowed by default, confirming arrows are excluded from requirements. - invalid tests include: - Missing @story on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature, with explicit checks on messageId "missingStory", error data (name/functionName), and exact autofix output. - Additional suites: - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" validate exported-only enforcement. - "require-story-annotation with scope option" validates that only configured node types are enforced. - tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts: - JSDoc header ties tests to docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md and relevant REQ IDs. - runAnnotationCheckerTests is used to validate TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature via the shared annotation-checker helper. - valid tests cover functions, function expressions, methods, and TS cases with @req, plus varied scope/exportPriority configurations. - invalid tests cover missing @req on: - Plain and annotated-only-with-@story FunctionDeclaration. - Function expressions (named variable, anonymous IIFE). - Class and object methods. - TS FunctionExpressions (exported and non-exported). - Numerous combinations for scope and exportPriority; all expect messageId "missingReq" with data { name, functionName }. - tests/utils/annotation-checker.test.ts further exercises TypeScript-specific behavior and autofix for missing @req.
Plugin integration: - src/index.ts lists both "require-story-annotation" and "require-req-annotation" in RULE_NAMES and dynamically requires ./rules/${name}, ensuring the rules are exposed by the plugin. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps both rules to severity "error", and they are included in the recommended/strict configs, satisfying the integration aspect of the story.
Test execution: - npm test -- --verbose was executed in this environment, which invoked `jest --ci --bail --verbose` as defined in package.json. No failures or stack traces appeared in the captured output; combined with the presence of extensive RuleTester suites for the two rules, this indicates tests for this story are implemented and runnable.
traceability.notes: The `require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation` rules are fully implemented and integrated, sharing a common function detection, scope, and exportPriority model and using robust, shared parsing logic for JSDoc and surrounding comments. They enforce @story and @req on the same set of function-like constructs (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature) while explicitly excluding arrow functions from traceability requirements by default. Error messages are clear, actionable, and anchored on the function or method name, and detection helpers are written defensively to handle malformed JSDoc and edge cases without breaking lint runs. TypeScript-specific constructs are supported and covered by tests. Rule documentation exists for both rules with configuration details and concrete examples. Comprehensive RuleTester test suites validate behavior for JavaScript, TypeScript, configuration options, and error messaging. Based on this concrete evidence, the story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is assessed as fully implemented and PASSED.
